subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this bootstrap-context event-loop mitigation now despite the custom glob-walker compatibility and prompt-context ordering tradeoffs?
rationale: The patch is a focused, well-covered mitigation for a P1 event-loop stall, but it changes a hot bootstrap context path whose glob semantics and ordering can affect existing configs and session prompt bytes; automation cannot own that upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Accept bounded mitigation
options.body: Land after maintainer review, accepting the full-walk/no-cap and walker-order behavior as the right tradeoff for avoiding event-loop stalls.

options.title: Require stronger live proof
options.body: Ask for a live embedded_run or channel-connected proof showing gateway/channel responsiveness under a broad bootstrap-extra-files glob before merge.

options.title: Narrow traversal semantics first
options.body: Require a pre-merge adjustment such as deterministic match ordering or a maintainer-approved traversal budget before accepting the custom glob replacement.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded mitigation
recommendation.body: Land after maintainer review, accepting the full-walk/no-cap and walker-order behavior as the right tradeoff for avoiding event-loop stalls.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the bootstrap read, bootstrap hook, and internal hook architecture touched by the tradeoff.
